idea: Make the ralph-overview snapshot that agents read (via MCP overview_parallel_ready_tasks and .ralph-overview/generated/snapshot.json) reliably FRESH, so the bookkeeper never plans a batch from stale data. Observed 2026-06-06: the MCP returned 40 ready tasks, 28 already merged/archived, and omitted same-day filings because the snapshot is only regenerated by a watcher/one-shot sync that was not running. Design axes: (1) MCP sync-on-read; (2) MCP server owns the watcher; (3) staleness guard; (4) sync-on-write. data.json lifecycle is the authoritative field the bookkeeper needs; the heavy job-state-derived stage fields are secondary and can stay watcher-updated.

candidateDirections.name: Lifecycle-first sync-on-read + staleness guard
candidateDirections.summary: Read data.json fresh per call as the authoritative task-set + lifecycle spine inside overview.parallel_ready_tasks; exclude lifecycle merged/archived as a hard invariant; include same-day filings absent from the snapshot via initialStage/prompts; overlay snapshot Ralph stage/dependency data only as enrichment; return snapshotAgeMs + a stale reason. Reuses existing getOverviewData() and snapshotStaleSince. Sub-second, not the ~17s full sync.

candidateDirections.name: MCP-owned watcher as background accelerator (harden existing WatcherSupervisor), not source of truth
candidateDirections.summary: Keep/harden the MCP WatcherSupervisor cold-start so heavier stage/dependency fields stay warm over a session, but treat it as a cache warmer rather than the correctness mechanism. Secondary to D-001 because a fresh snapshot still returns merged tasks via the call-path lifecycle gap.

candidateDirections.name: Snapshot freshness contract + sync-on-write hook (convenience layer only)
candidateDirections.summary: Add an explicit snapshot freshness/age contract and a post-edit sync-on-write hook after data.json changes. Insufficient as a correctness boundary (misses manual edits, merges, branch switches, failed hooks); a staleness guard alone also fails because the tool still returns stale readyTasks. Full sync-on-read is rejected on latency. At most a convenience layer behind D-001.

questionsForSynthesis: When data.json is newer than snapshot.json, should overview.parallel_ready_tasks return lifecycle-correct results with a warning, or fail closed unless allowStale is passed?
Should overview.parallel_ready_tasks ever return a lifecycle merged/archived task regardless of Ralph stage? (Recommend making 'no' a tested invariant with stale-snapshot fixtures.)
For newly-filed tasks absent from the snapshot, what minimal readiness semantics are acceptable: initialStage + command.prompts only, blockedOn from data.json, or full PRD/dependencyGraph derivation?
Should snapshotAgeMs / snapshotStaleSince be elevated from advisory metadata to a hard warning in the tool result prose so agents cannot silently plan from stale dynamic fields?
Was the 2026-06-06 incident partly caused by an older marketplace build without the WatcherSupervisor, vs the call-path lifecycle gap (even if both, the call-path gap is real)?
